title: Unit normalization of the proper/open restriction identification
statement: Let Λ be a finite commutative ring, f:T1→T2 a proper morphism of schemes, and j1:X→T1 and j2:X→T2 open immersions with j1 f=j2. Work in the bounded-below ordinary étale derived categories with constant Λ-module coefficients [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let θ:j2^* Rf_* j1! K ≅ K be exactly the identification of [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison]. Let η1 be the unit of j1! ⊣ j1^*, εf the counit of f^* ⊣ Rf_*, and a:j2^* ≅ j1^* f^* the canonical inverse-image composition identification. Then, for every K in D⁺(X_et,Λ), θ.hom followed by η1(K) equals a.hom(Rf_* j1!K) followed by j1^*(εf(j1!K)). No Cartesian condition on the square with j1,j2,f and id_X is assumed.

proof.text: Put V = T1 ×[T2] X, with projections b and p, and s=(j1,id). Then s b=j1 and s p=id. The section is clopen. Expand the specified theta as the derived pullback exchange, Rp_* of extension-by-zero base change (including the identity pullback comparison), and the characterized clopen component restriction.

proof.text: Use the equation characterizing clopenSectionDirectImage: its component hom followed by the open-extension unit is Rp_* of the s^* ⊣ Rs_* unit followed by the direct-image compositor and identity comparison. Identify its termwise extension unit with the derived adjunction unit by the localization factorization equations on bounded-below complexes. Naturality moves open base change through this unit; its defining mate equation identifies its transpose with the inverse-image compositor for s b=j1. Thus theta followed by the j1 unit is restriction of the pullback exchange along s.

proof.text: Write the derived exchange as a mate. Its counit equation identifies restriction along s with the inverse-image compositor for j1 f=j2 followed by j1^* of the derived counit for f. The direct-image and inverse-image compositors are conjugate, so their factors for s p=id cancel by the adjunction identities and identity normalizations. These are exactly the two displayed factors on the right. This proof does not require the refinement square to be Cartesian, density, nonempty X or a nonzero coefficient ring. The section cancellation used here can be isolated as follows. For adjunctions Lp ⊣ Rp and Ls ⊣ Rs, an isomorphism e:Id ≅ Lp followed by Ls, and rho:Rs followed by Rp ≅ Id conjugate to e, one has homEquiv_p(v) followed by Rp(eta_s) followed by rho = e.hom followed by Ls(v). Naturality of eta_s, then naturality of rho, reduces this equality to unit_conjugateEquiv for the composite adjunction. This generic identity has been checked in Lean. Apply it with the p and s inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions; the isomorphism e comes from s p=id. The remaining Lean formalization is transporting the specified geometric theta through the open base-change and derived-unit identifications.

theorem properOpenIdentification_unit
    (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ]
    {T₁ T₂ X : Scheme.{u}} (f : T₁ ⟶ T₂) [IsProper f]
    (j₁ : X ⟶ T₁) (j₂ : X ⟶ T₂) [IsOpenImmersion j₁] [IsOpenImmersion j₂]
    (h : j₁ ≫ f = j₂)
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))) :
    (properOpenIdentification Λ f j₁ j₂ h K).hom ≫
        (derivedOpenImmersionLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunctionPlus
          (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j₁).unit.app K =
      (upperStarCompDerivedPlus (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j₁ f j₂ h.symm).hom.app
          ((rightDerivedLowerStarPlus (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) f).obj
            ((openImmersionLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j₁).mapDerivedCategoryPlus.obj K)) ≫
        (upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j₁).mapDerivedCategoryPlus.map
          ((upperStarLowerStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) f).derivedPlus.counit.app
            ((openImmersionLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j₁).mapDerivedCategoryPlus.obj
              K))
